title: Scope server lifecycle derivation to the entity's lab step list
body:
## Summary
The server-side lifecycle derivation (headless.ts derivedByEntity/totalStepsFor) counts every persisted artifact row against a denominator of only the registered pipeline's steps, while the lab counts against registry + bespoke labels; 9 of 160 entities with artifacts derive a lifecycle their own in-list rows do not support.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/headless.ts:291 totalStepsFor returns stepsForProfile(pipeline).length (11 for items) and src/lib/catalog/headless.ts:302 derivedByEntity passes ALL of the entity's rows to deriveEntityLifecycle, so the 7 bespoke Items labels (src/lib/catalog/acceptance/itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:279, graded server-side via stepGradability) inflate produced/passed against a denominator that excludes them. The lab uses catalogManifest bespokeStepEntries (src/components/layout-lab/catalogManifest.ts:164) = 18 labels for items. Result: items/item-1 evidence reads 'produced 14/11' and lifecycle 'generated' while its in-list rows give 'scaffolded'; 8 saber/crystal items read 'scaffolded' from a lone bespoke 'Attributes' row. Fixed = one server-importable per-entity step list (profile-scoped registered labels + the catalog's bespoke labels) used for both the denominator and the row filter. Needs an exported bespoke label list from acceptance/stepGradability.ts (catalog-acceptance's path), hence out of scope this round.

## Flow
- probe on a copy of ~/.pof/pof.db: deriveCatalogLifecycle(c) vs deriveEntityLifecycle(rows filtered to the entity's step labels)
- export bespokeStepLabels(catalogId) from acceptance/stepGradability.ts
- headless.ts: entity step labels = profile-scoped registered labels + bespoke labels; filter rows by them and use their count as totalSteps
- re-run the probe: mismatches vs the lab step list -> 0

## Expected impact
MCP/headless callers (pof_list_entities, lifecycle sync, the catalog_lifecycle cache) stop reporting produced > total and a lifecycle the lab does not show for Items entities. The next sync may rewrite catalog_lifecycle for those 9 entities (a re-derivable cache).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - server lifecycle agrees with the lab's step list
Before: 9 of 160 entities with artifacts derive a lifecycle/produced count their in-list rows do not support (items/item-1: produced 14/11, generated vs scaffolded); 15 of 805 rows counted outside the pipeline list
After: 0 of 160 mismatches against the lab's registry+bespoke list (predicted)
Method: simulation - Before measured by a probe on a DB copy; After needs the stepGradability export in catalog-acceptance's paths, not ownable this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/headless.ts:291-315
src/components/layout-lab/catalogManifest.ts:164-173
probe (2026-11-08, DB copy): {entities:160, mismatch:9, rows:805, orphanRows:15}
items/item-1: server=generated produced=14/11 scoped=scaffolded produced=7 orphans=3D Generation|Animations|Attributes|Inventory UI Integration|Material / Texture|SFX|VFX
instrument: DB-copy probe: count entities whose deriveCatalogLifecycle lifecycle/produced differs from a derivation over rows filtered to catalogManifest(catalogId).steps scoped by profile; Before 9, After must be 0

title: Implement or retract the presentation-binding convention PIPELINE_REVIEW states
body:
## Summary
docs/catalog/PIPELINE_REVIEW.md:95 says presentation steps bind to a shared presentation-catalog entry via presentationLink; src/lib/catalog/presentation-links.ts has zero importers outside its own test.

## Description
PIPELINE_REVIEW.md:95: 'Presentation steps become bindings. Icon/VFX/SFX/Music/Ambient steps on content rows bind to a shared presentation-catalog entry (presentationLink) - produced once.' src/lib/catalog/presentation-links.ts:31 presentationLink and :10 PRESENTATION_CATALOGS are consumed only by src/__tests__/lib/catalog/presentation-links.test.ts; no pipeline, seed or step reads them, so every content entity still produces its own VFX/SFX/Icon steps. Either the convention is adopted (pipelines bind through it) or the doc line and the module are retracted. Which one is a product decision about the pipeline's shape, so it is human.

## Flow
- grep src for presentationLink|PRESENTATION_CATALOGS|isPresentationCatalog -> only presentation-links.ts and its test
- decide: adopt (wire content pipelines' presentation steps to bindings) or retract (delete module + test, edit PIPELINE_REVIEW.md:95)

## Expected impact
A pipeline author reading the review doc stops expecting a binding mechanism that does not exist. Retracting deletes 34 LOC + a test; adopting is a multi-catalog change.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the doc claim matches the code
Before: 1 documented convention, 0 production consumers of presentation-links.ts
After: 0 doc claims without code (either path)
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep; the adopt-vs-retract choice has no figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Delete the retired StepSpec.copy field and its dead read branch
body:
## Summary
StepSpec.copy is documented RETIRED (spec-linter rule (l) forbids authoring it; 0 registered steps author it) but the field is still declared and genericFixCopy.ts still reads it.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/stepSpec.ts:211-232 says it is 'Still declared only because withGenericFixCopy reads it; with rule (l) green that branch is provably dead and should be deleted the next time that file is touched.' src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/genericFixCopy.ts:139 `spec.copy?.(data) ?? genericFixCopy(base, spec)` is that branch; src/__tests__/catalog/pipeline-spec-linter.test.ts:497 pins zero authors. Fixed = drop the field, the branch and the comments naming StepSpec.copy as an override (genericFixCopy.ts:15,89); rule (l) then becomes a type error instead of a lint. genericFixCopy.ts is catalog-browser-ui's path, so out of scope this round.

## Flow
- remove `copy?:` from StepSpec (stepSpec.ts:232); StepFixCopy stays as genericFixCopy's return type
- genericFixCopy.ts:139 -> genericFixCopy(base, spec)
- typecheck: any authored copy becomes a compile error; spec-linter rule (l) stays green

## Expected impact
Removes one dead optional field from the contract ~344 steps implement; nothing user-visible. Could break an out-of-tree spec authoring copy (none in tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead contract surface removed
Before: 1 declared field + 1 read branch + 2 doc mentions; 0 registered steps author it
After: 0; typecheck green
Method: probe - grep of authors (linter rule l) and readers (genericFixCopy.ts:139); the edit sits in catalog-browser-ui's file
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: typecheck + pipeline-spec-linter.test.ts green after removing the field; grep 'spec.copy' in src returns 0

title: Derive RECIPE_MODULE from CATALOG_MODULE instead of a second hand list
body:
## Summary
recipe.ts keeps its own catalog->module map (10 entries) that duplicates the declared single source CATALOG_MODULE and disagrees with it on currencies.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/catalog-module.ts:9 CATALOG_MODULE calls itself the single source of truth for catalog->owning module and maps currencies -> arpg-inventory (via NEW_CATALOGS, src/lib/catalog/new-catalogs.ts:104). src/lib/catalog/recipe.ts:46 RECIPE_MODULE re-lists 10 of those pairs verbatim and omits currencies, with a comment that 'Currency has no domain-scoped module' - contradicting the single source. The recipe map scopes which UE gotchas and knowledge tips a generation prompt carries, so the two answers to 'which module owns currencies' differ by surface. Fixed = moduleForRecipe reads CATALOG_MODULE with an explicit, commented exclusion set if currencies must keep the superset.

## Flow
- diff RECIPE_MODULE against CATALOG_MODULE: 10 identical, 1 disagreement (currencies)
- decide currencies (superset vs arpg-inventory) and record it as an explicit exclusion
- replace the hand map; golden-prompt check for the 11 recipe catalogs

## Expected impact
Generation prompts and session labelling agree on a catalog's module, and a new recipe catalog needs one edit instead of two. A changed currencies scope would change its prompt header.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one catalog->module answer
Before: 2 hand maps, 10 duplicated entries, 1 disagreement
After: 1 map + explicit exclusions; recipe prompts byte-identical for the 10 agreeing catalogs
Method: probe - entry-by-entry diff of the two maps; prompt equality needs a golden harness over getRecipe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: snapshot getRecipe(c).buildPrompt for the 11 recipe catalogs before/after; 10 identical, the currencies diff reviewed
